A low-angle full-body shot captures a young adult female-presenting subject, approximately in her early 20s, with extremely pale, porcelain skin and very light, platinum-blond hair—features suggesting a Northern European or albino appearance—standing statuesque on a rocky foreground. She wears sculpted metallic armor-like adornments: a reflective, contoured metal bra with hammered texture and tiny pendant chains, articulated forearm pieces and ornate metal gloves encrusted with filigree, and oversized, high-shine silver trousers that read like liquid metal or laminated vinyl, their surfaces creased with deep specular highlights and sharp fold lines; additional chains and dangling jewelry drape across her hips and torso, adding a fine, beaded texture against bare skin. A small dark tattoo is visible on her left ribcage. The setting is a brooding coastal scene with a massive, curling ocean wave frozen behind her—the surf rendered with smooth, photographic motion that softens toward the horizon—against a dark, almost monochrome sky. Lighting is dramatic and highly specular: strong high-key rim light from above and slightly behind creates bright highlights on the glossy metals and hair, producing crisp specular reflections and subtle subsurface scattering on the skin at the cheeks and shoulders; shadows are cool and diffuse with soft falloff, and there are faint bloom/halation effects around the brightest edges. Dominant colors are metallic silver, slate gray, and desaturated cool blues, with skin and hair registering as pale creams and near-white highlights. Framing is heroic and centered, shot from a low, slightly wide-angle perspective that emphasizes leg length and the imposing stance, with a moderately deep focus that keeps both subject and the near wave detail relatively sharp while allowing the distant sea to soften; there is minimal motion blur and no significant chromatic aberration, though post-processed glow and clarity enhancements are evident. The image quality suggests high-resolution digital capture heavily retouched or composited—likely a modern digital editorial or CGI-assisted fashion photograph—with visible digital sharpening, smooth skin retouching, and subtle noise reduction that gives an almost hyperreal finish. At the bottom center, a small stylized mark resembling the letters "JP" is visible as a signature or logo. The overall mood is otherworldly and commanding—icy, futuristic, and elegiac with a stylized, cinematic tension between organic vulnerability and gleaming, armor-like adornment.

There are absolutely no 90-degree overhead shots, no "cooking tutorial" camera angles hovering directly above the food, and no flat compositions—if the frame only shows the countertop and hands without any foreground depth, then the camera angle is wrong. The forearms always extend from the bottom edge of the frame and into the depth of the frame, with realistic perspective shortening. A sharp cut only changes the time, never the viewpoint: after each sharp cut, the frame remains in the line of sight of those eyes, just jumping to the next moment. The entire film contains absolutely no third-person shots, no shots of the chef from the side or opposite, no over-the-shoulder shots, and no shots showing the chef's figure—the chef's face and body never appear in a single frame, not even in the reflections of the knife blade, the refrigerator glass, or the bar counter's paint. After each sharp cut, the hands must be in action within the frame; there are no empty shots without hands. The hands of a middle-aged craftsman: well-defined knuckles, clean and firm, a thin callus on the second joint of the right index finger, very short nails, and the cuffs of his navy blue work clothes rolled up to the middle of his forearm. Every detail remains perfectly consistent between each cut. Camera movement is always generated by his body—bending over, turning, looking up; the camera never moves independently of the body. The footage allows and requires all the imperfections of authentic first-person video: slight shakiness, tilt, overshoot, imperfect composition.

Operational visibility lock: The pinching motion must be designed for the camera: hands raised to the lower right of chest level, about 40 cm from eyes—hands raised towards the line of sight, not eyes hovering directly above the hands; even at this close range, the depth of the bar counter is still visible at the top edge of the frame. The back of the hand never completely obscures the sushi being formed—the workpiece is always within a visible gap between the hands. After each squeeze, the fingers must open for a moment, allowing the forming rice tray or whole piece of sushi to be fully exposed on the fingers, facing the line of sight; at every crucial moment of swishing, flipping, and shaping, the sushi itself is clearly visible in the frame. The movement from the palm to the wooden counter is a complete and visible arc: the palm opens, the sushi lies on the fingers, it's placed on the counter, and gently set down—the moment of contact is clearly visible, never obscured by the back of the hand.

Continuity Lock: Only items clearly placed in the previous shot are present on the cutting board, wooden counter, and rice table; nothing more, nothing less. The number of sushi on the wooden counter is a strictly increasing counter: 0 pieces → 1 piece → 2 pieces → 3 pieces. Each increment must be a clearly visible placement action within the frame—no sushi will ever appear on the counter without being placed on camera. At the start of each shot, the state of everything (including the exact number on the counter) must be completely consistent with the end of the previous shot. Every action occurs only once in the entire film—washing hands once, checking the knife once, cutting each piece of fish only once, pinching each piece only once—never repeated. Format Mode: Controlled multi-shot sequence, real-time speed, using only hard cuts. A hard cut is a jump in time, not a change in camera position—the same pair of eyes are looking before and after the cut. Each segment begins with action in progress, the hands already in the frame—no empty frames, no fixed shots, no dissolves. Action Rhythm 1 – Opening Ceremony: A continuous, uninterrupted shot shows him looking down at his hands. Optics and Camera: The entire film uses a single "lens": his eyes, positioned about 50 centimeters above and behind his hands, gazing downwards at approximately a 40-degree angle—a perpetually oblique perspective, always conveying forward depth, with no vertical overhead shots or instructional video camera angles. A fixed 47° diagonal field of view is presented within a relatively wide tempo, tightening during the fish-cutting and shaping stages due to the forward lean—the changes in framing only come from the body's genuine forward lean and bending, never from zooming or changing camera positions. The head posture during the shaping segments naturally serves visibility: chin slightly tucked, gaze passing over fingertips onto the workpiece—precisely the true working gaze of a craftsman. The unconscious swaying of the standing body, the slow shifting of weight between the feet, the subtle rise and fall with each breath; the long pull of the knife and the moment of each shaping almost freeze the image, leaving only a slight tremor of breath, followed by a relaxed, gentle sway. Every shift in gaze is a genuine head turn: a quick start, a slight overshoot followed by correction, and stabilization with aftershock. No gimbal for smooth movement, no electronic stabilization, no uniform camera movement, no fisheye lens, no lens changes, no zoom. Physics: Hyper-realistic physics, with the realism of the fish meat as the highest priority: Yellowtail is soft biological tissue, not a geometric shape—the pale pinkish-white surface undulates with the muscle texture, the white fascia curves, the edges are rounded and irregular; when the knife passes over it, the tissue separates along the grain, slightly sinks and springs back, the cut surface is moist and reflective. The Yanagiba knife is a single piece of rigid steel—highest priority: the blade is absolutely straight, never bent, never broken, never deformed in any frame of the film; the outline from the base to the tip is always a continuous line. When wiping the knife, the cloth, not the knife, bears the force: the cloth slides along the plane of the knife and deforms slightly, while the knife itself remains completely still, like wiping a fixed steel rail. The knife exists in only two states: held in the hand, or laid flat on a knife rest/cutting board (blade facing outwards)—never suspended in mid-air, never piercing fabric or fingers. A three-millimeter-thin slice of fish, when picked up, droops softly like silk, its edges slightly translucent; when placed on a rice tray, it drapes gracefully along the sides, its thickness remaining constant from cut to consumption—never right angles, never machine-cut flatness, never artificially thickening. The vinegared rice, when pressed between the fingers, shows visible firmness, each grain distinct and not mushy; wasabi leaves a pale green mark on the fish's back; soy sauce brushes across the fish's surface, giving it a subtle sheen; yuzu peel crumbs have a realistic, minute weight settling on the fish; when placed on the wooden counter, the bottom of the sushi sinks slightly against the wood. The tendons in both hands are visible, reflecting the true strength of the knife grip and finger positioning. Nothing floats, deforms, replicates, or penetrates the mold.

A young woman with pale blonde hair swept into a low bun stands in a cold, teal-lit night office, a dark corded telephone against her ear, wearing an oversized pale-blue tee over a grey shirt while cubicle partitions and glowing blue monitors recede behind her. From the black gap between the partitions lurches an emaciated, screaming creature with wet stringy hair, a filthy stained tank top, grime-smeared skin, and a beaded bracelet, driving toward her in a predatory rush. The sequence follows a survival arc in a Zack Snyder register: real-time contact ramping hard into a bullet-time freeze, one clean 360-degree horizontal orbit at constant angular velocity, then a snap back to real time where the creature is instantly on her again and she barely reaches a glass door in time. The environment escalates from a stable workspace into a toppling chair, scattered papers, and one flickering fluorescent tube, while the sickly cyan and cold monitor blue hold their exact color throughout. During the freeze the entire room becomes a solid sculpture and only the camera moves; the frozen fall is the sequence's single speed event.
Single continuous shot 30s: The camera holds a low medium framing on the woman as she lowers the handset, then eases back and left just as the creature erupts from the dark gap behind her, its screaming face catching the cold fluorescent light. The instant its grimy hand lands on her shoulder and her weight pitches backward, the speed ramps hard out of real time into a total freeze [VFX: bullet-time time-stop, everything frozen mid-air — the woman suspended in her backward fall, the torn-loose handset floating on its taut cord, papers hanging in a fixed scatter, the creature locked mid-lunge, dust motes stopped, monitors still glowing]. Now moving as a high-speed robotic arm, the camera begins low and behind her left shoulder and carries one unbroken 360-degree horizontal revolution around her suspended body at a single constant angular velocity, neither accelerating nor pausing, while it rises with extreme slowness from the low upward angle to her eye level, keeping her whole falling form full in frame as it passes the frozen creature, the fixed papers, and the blue monitor glow, every element holding its exact position throughout the circle. As the orbit completes in front of her, time resumes with a violent snap: she slams to the floor and the creature is already lunging down onto her, so she scrambles backward on her hands, kicks off the toppling chair, and hauls herself up as the camera whip-tracks with her sprint, the creature clawing right at her back through the flickering light. She hits the glass office door a stride ahead of it and throws her whole weight through, and as she wrenches it shut the creature's body slams the glass a half-second too late; the camera pushes to a tight framing on her gasping face pressed to the door while its pale hands and screaming mouth smear against the other side.

30-second short film, 16:9, entirely first-person POV, with the ultra-photorealistic look and texture of live-action footage.

Japan, 2010. A rainy blue-hour evening. A warm, lived-in family kitchen at night. A mother calmly prepares several traditional Japanese dishes at once, including chirashi sushi, grilled fish, and miso soup. Her movements are practiced, efficient, and completely unhurried—an ordinary domestic routine portrayed with natural realism.

The film consists of exactly eight shots connected only by clean, sharp HARD CUTS. No transition effects, dissolves, fade-ins, or fade-outs.

CRITICAL POV RULE FOR EVERY SHOT

Every shot is seen exclusively through the eyes of the same mother. There are no observer angles, no third-person shots, and no exterior view of her body or face. Changes in shot scale come only from where she looks and how close her body moves to something: looking down at her hands creates a close view; raising her eyes toward the living room creates a distant view; leaning toward a pot creates an extreme close-up.

Time moves continuously forward across all eight shots.

CAMERA AND VIEWPOINT FOR THE ENTIRE FILM

The camera is the eyesight of a Japanese mother, approximately 35 years old, standing inside the open counter-style kitchen of a small suburban Japanese home. She stands on the kitchen side of the preparation counter. A waist-high counter separates her from the dining area, living room, and the large window at the far end of the home.

Adult female eye level, approximately 157 cm above the floor. Rectilinear wide-angle perspective equivalent to approximately 24mm. Straight architectural lines with natural perspective. No fisheye distortion, no GoPro look, and no barrel distortion. Natural head movement, subtle breathing sway, and gentle human micro-motion.

Her face never appears. Only her hands, forearms, thin wedding ring, and the lower edge of her pale-blue apron may enter the frame.

CONTINUITY LOCK FOR EVERY SHOT

The same home, kitchen layout, lighting, clothing, tableware, cookware, food, and props remain perfectly consistent throughout the film. Character positions change only through continuous story movement.

The household has exactly four members: the mother, whose eyes are the camera; her husband; their older son; and their young daughter. The mother is the only adult woman in the home.

Beyond the kitchen counter, the older son, approximately ten years old, leans over the dining table doing homework. In the living room, the five-year-old daughter, wearing pajamas with her hair in twin ponytails, sits close to a heavy CRT television watching an animated program. Flickering blue television light washes across the room. A warm yellow floor lamp glows in the back of the living room. Beyond it is a short hallway leading to the entrance. Outside the large window, deep indigo twilight fills the rainy evening, with streams of rainwater running down the glass.

On the kitchen counter: a wooden hangiri sushi-rice tub filled with glossy vinegared rice, a wooden rice paddle, a round hand fan, a cutting board covered with fine golden kinshi tamago egg ribbons, small dishes containing sweet snow peas and thin slices of lotus root, a small dish of salmon roe, several green shiso leaves, and a tray holding thick slices of tamagoyaki.

On the stove, a small pot of miso soup gently bubbles. Salt-grilled mackerel sizzles inside the built-in fish grill. The rice cooker glows with an orange indicator light and releases small pulses of steam.

A cream-colored wall-mounted telephone typical of Japan around 2010 hangs on the wall. Its handset is attached by a long coiled cord. A paper calendar also hangs nearby.

All spoken dialogue is in Japanese exactly as written below, delivered slowly and casually in a relaxed domestic rhythm, with natural pauses between phrases.

SHOT 1 — 0–4 SECONDS — SHE LOOKS DOWN AT HER OWN HANDS

Her hands fill the lower foreground above the wooden rice tub. Her left hand gently fans the vinegared rice while her right hand uses the wooden rice paddle to cut, fold, and loosen it. Individual rice grains glisten with vinegar as faint steam drifts upward.

She briefly raises her eyes over the counter, glancing at her son doing homework and her daughter sitting in front of the television. Her gaze naturally returns to her hands.

HARD CUT.

SHOT 2 — 4–8 SECONDS — SHE STANDS IN FRONT OF THE WALL TELEPHONE AND WATCHES HER HAND TAKE THE RECEIVER

The wall-mounted telephone rings with the classic trembling cadence of a Japanese home telephone:

「プルルルル、プルルルル」

Two rings, then a pause.

Her hand lifts the receiver from its cradle and raises it to her ear. The hand holding the receiver remains visible along the right edge of the frame near her ear. The long coiled cord stretches from the wall and gently springs and sways.

She speaks slowly and casually:

「あ、もしもし。……ごめんね、いま夕飯作ってて。あとでかけ直すね」

She returns the receiver to its cradle with a small mechanical click.

HARD CUT.

SHOT 3 — 8–11 SECONDS — SHE LOOKS DOWN AT HER DAUGHTER BESIDE HER

She turns back toward the counter and lowers her gaze. Her little daughter has quietly slipped into the kitchen. The girl stands on tiptoe, one small hand hovering above the tray of tamagoyaki. She freezes, then raises her large eyes and looks directly up at “us.”

The mother gently scolds her with an amused smile in her voice:

「こーら。まだだめよ」

The girl pouts, then runs away beneath the lower edge of the frame, her feet thumping softly across the floor.

HARD CUT.

SHOT 4 — 11–15 SECONDS — SHE LEANS CLOSE TO THE STOVE, BRINGING HER EYES NEAR THE FOOD

Her hand pulls open the fish-grill drawer. The skin of the salt-grilled mackerel is blistered, browned, and sizzling. Using long cooking chopsticks, she turns the fish over and slides the grill drawer closed again.

She immediately bends forward and lowers her head toward the miso-soup pot. The viewpoint physically descends with her head until the bubbling surface of the soup fills most of her vision.

Hot steam rises directly into the camera. The lower edge of the image briefly fogs and softens before slowly clearing.

She gives a quiet, satisfied hum:

「ん〜」

HARD CUT.

SHOT 5 — 15–19 SECONDS — SHE RAISES HER EYES TOWARD THE ENTRANCE, THEN GLANCES SIDEWAYS

The front door opens in the distant hallway.

Her husband, nearly forty, appears with rain dampening the shoulders of his business suit. He closes his umbrella and shakes off the water.

He calls:

「ただいま〜」

Both children answer together:

「おかえり〜！」

He walks around the end of the counter and enters the kitchen, approaching her from the peripheral edge of “our” field of view. He lowers his head slightly, his gaze directed toward her temple. The side of his face briefly enters the extreme edge of the frame as he places a gentle kiss on her temple, then steps back.

She lets out a soft, happy laugh.

He lifts the lid of the soup pot, leans in to smell it, and says:

「ん、いい匂い」

He replaces the lid and walks toward the hallway.

HARD CUT.

SHOT 6 — 19–23 SECONDS — SHE LOOKS DOWN AT HER DAUGHTER GAZING UP AT HER

The little girl stands beside her again, looking upward with both hands hidden behind her back. She speaks slowly and with deliberate politeness:

「ママ、ひとつちょうだい？……おねがいします」

The mother laughs gently and answers:

「じょうずに言えたね。はい、はしっこどうぞ」

Her hand enters the frame holding a small, cooled end piece of tamagoyaki. She places it into the girl’s waiting hands.

The girl receives it with both hands and says:

「ありがとう！」

She takes a small bite and runs out of the frame.

HARD CUT.

SHOT 7 — 23–26 SECONDS — SHE LOOKS DOWN AT HER HANDS ABOVE THE RICE TUB

Her hands move quickly but elegantly as she completes the chirashi sushi. She spreads the fine golden egg ribbons evenly across the vinegared rice. She places bright green snow peas and clean white lotus-root slices one by one, building distinct layers of natural color across the surface.

HARD CUT.

SHOT 8 — 26–30 SECONDS — SHE BENDS DEEPLY OVER THE RICE TUB UNTIL ONLY THE CHIRASHI SUSHI FILLS HER VIEW

The surface of the chirashi sushi is extremely close to her eyes. Very shallow depth of field isolates the food details.

She briefly holds her breath.

The tips of her long chopsticks lift several translucent beads of salmon roe. She places them individually in the exact center of the dish. Each orange pearl catches the light with a glossy, jewel-like sheen.

She lifts a single fresh green shiso leaf and lowers it beside the salmon roe with extremely gentle, millimeter-level precision. The leaf veins are sharply visible, and its tip trembles slightly as the chopsticks release it.

She exhales softly. A faint breath of warm vapor brushes across the lens.

The film ends on this exact close-up as a clean held final frame. No fade-out.

Use only authentic diegetic location sound recorded as if captured inside the real room. Absolutely no music and no score. The room tone and environmental audio continue naturally across every hard cut without interruption.

prompt_bank.name: Static shot
prompt_bank.prompt: The camera stays planted in one immovable position from the first frame to the last. Zero motion — no drift, no shake, no breathing, no stabilization float, no micro-drift; absolute rock-solid stillness throughout. Angle, elevation, distance to the scene and the overall composition are frozen and never altered; every ounce of motion comes from the scene itself, never from the camera. The clip closes on precisely the framing it began with, identical down to the pixel.

prompt_bank.name: Pan right
prompt_bank.prompt: Rotate the camera horizontally from left to right from one fixed point, like a standing head-turn, starting on [composition A] and sweeping across [the environment]; no sideways travel, no dolly, no truck, no arc, no slide, no zoom, no tilt. Speed: smooth constant rotation, decelerating gently at the end. Framing: keep the horizon level while new space enters from the right side of the frame only through rotation; [the landing subject] stays beyond the right edge until the rotation brings them in. End: settle on a clear final composition on [the landing subject] and hold.

prompt_bank.name: Tilt up
prompt_bank.prompt: Fixed camera position at [lens height]. The tilt starts on [the lower anchor] and finishes framing [the subject] in the upper third, decelerating into a static hold.
